                                       I.      INTRODUCTION

       The Commission and AJLs should and have the ability and precedence to DENY the Joint

Application per PURA §37.056 (b) (3) of Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC (Oncor) and

Lower Colorado River Authority Transmission Service Corporation (LCRA TSC) (collectively,

the Applicants) to Amend their Certificates of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) for the Bell

County East to Big Hill Substation 765-kV Transmission Line Project in Bell, Burnet, Concho,

Tom Green, and Williamson Counties (The 59475 Application).

       Additionally, because of SOAH Order 24 (59182) and Order 12 (59475), the Commission

and AJLs should and have the ability and precedence to DENY the Joint Application per PURA

§37.056 (b) (3) of Oncor Electric Delivery Company, LLC (Oncor) and Lower Colorado River

Authority Transmission Service Corporation (LCRA TSC) (collectively, the Applicants) to

Amend their Certificates of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) for Big Hill Substation to Sand

Lake Switch 765-kV Transmission Line Project in Crane, Crockett, Irion, Pecos, Reagan, Reeves,

Schleicher, Tom Green, Upton, and Ward (The 59182 Application).

     The Applicants failed to present factual and accurate data to the evidentiary record, and they

do not demonstrate compliance with the requirements of Public Utility Regulatory Act (PURA)

§37.056 or HB 5066. The Applicants have failed to demonstrate complete evidence on record that

would compel the Public Utility Commission (Commission) to grant the Applicants the supreme

privilege to construct the size and scale of this type of public infrastructure project. Landowners

have not had sufficient time or opportunity to mount a defense of their properties in the 765 KV

cases. Additionally, an approval of this application “will open the door” for further challenges on

the State’s ability to confer eminent domain to private companies, due to the lack of due process

granted in the amended PURA §37.057 by the rapid 180 day approval process being in direct

violation to Landowners Due Course of Law, Due Process and §2001.051 & §2001.174 rights.

This would have far reaching consequences for the state beyond the scope of this project.

A.     Applicants’ Background Statement on Intervenors at hearings focused primarily on

       challenging routing and not “Need” at the Hearing is without Merit

        In the Applicants’ brief they stated that “Aside from certain parties at the Hearing on Merits

(“Hearing”) who contested the need for the Permian Basin Reliability as a whole, the issues

addressed at the Hearing related to routing preferences and constraints.”1 The lack of comment

or contest on “need” does not equal to a “thumbs up” on the project or suggest that people and

existing ERCOT/ONCOR/LCRA customers want this project.

        The Applicants suggests that few and certain parties at the Hearing contested the need and

implying the concept makes a green light for the project. To contest this suggestion, a look at the

inverse of this argument is required. Where are the few parties, if any, requesting the 765 KV

transmission line? The Applicants will point to the unsubstantiated Exhibit 33 – the Trade’s Memo

and the oil and gas industry, but the oil and gas industry didn’t stand up their argument with a PUC

attorney that argued the need in these proceedings, nor did they bother to write a public comment,

despite their justiciable interest in the project.2 The Applicants will point the datacenters as end-

users that need this project, however they too have not been a party to these proceedings. In this

hearing, we didn’t see the private company end-users that so desperately “need” the power put

forth a witness to testify their dire need for this “energy”. Equally none of the

intervenors/landowners were able to ask the end users questions in Hearing on Merits about the

merits of their specific energy needs and requirements or obtain evidence. No LCRA or Oncor

existing or future end-user customer showed up as a whole, to defend the need, quantify the need,

          I would ask the ALJs and Commission why is okay to deprive someone else their right to

  own and operate a business such as a Farm and Ranch operation for an unknown “need” in an

          What these parties did do was allegedly submit an unsigned, unsubstantiated letter (Exhibit

       Why did these interested parties not participate in the hearings? They have a justiciable

interest in these preceding outside the average rate payer. There is no evidence that supports the

need in these hearings from the end-users customers or “pro-need supporters”. The “one-time”

report from the ERCOT Permian Basin Reliability Plan (PBRP), presented with the Application

and a mischaracterization of HB 5066 and the amended law PURA §39.166-67, discussed in

McCulloughs’ Initial Brief, do not establish the need of the project, because at the basic premise

the PBRP is lacking established need statements of quantity of power, when it is need and where

it is needed.19




B.      Need

         As stated in the McCulloughs’ Initial Brief, The Applicants have not completed any

engineered studies to justify need, they rely solely on HB 5066 and ERCOT PBRP to point to the

need of the project. 20 The Applicants will say they weren’t required by Commission to do their

own study, however there is no evidence in Docket 57441 that points to this statement nor have

the Applicants pointed specifically where the Commission has said that no further reports are

needed for PBRP projects.21 However, if this project was so important to the Applicants they

would have proactively backed up the need with their own study as required, for burden of proof

since they are required to prove the need, quantifying the amount of power for each line and

substation, the location of the demand required, when the power is needed at each

                 In the Applicants’ Initial Brief, the Applicants quotes their own Application to point to

      their own directives of HB 5066 reliability plan instead of law in PURA §39.166-67. The 59475

      & 59182 Applications, they incorrectly insert the word “transmission” in the number (2) of the HB

      5066 directive, to justify the three (3) 765 KV Imports.23 However, transmission does not address

      the capacity directive in HB 5066 (2) address increasing available capacity, which is a generation

      directive. Transmission lines do not make power or increase capacity, they move electrons.

      Why would the legislature make a bill that addresses local transmission upgrades in the (1) and (3)

      directives of HB 5066 reliability plan requirements, with no directive to generate power? A full

      and complete reliability directive is local transmission with generation. The bill that created the

      Competitive Renewable Energy Zones (CREZ) lines Senate Bill 20 (2005) directed in codified

      PURA §39.904(k) state that “The commission and the independent organization certified for

      ERCOT shall study the need for increased transmission and generation capacity throughout this

      state (emphasis added).”24 This code from the CREZ lines shows the precedence and that it is

      appropriate for ERCOT to add generation to the study as required and it points to capacity being

      generation NOT transmission.
